name: Timeboxing and Calendar Blocking
diagnostic: Parkinson’s Law dynamics. Work expands elastically to fill the temporal space allocated for its completion if that duration is fluid or indefinite.

procedure.text: Pick the day's top one to three deliverables.
Estimate an aggressive but realistic duration for each, from its broken-down parts.
Put non-overlapping calendar blocks on the calendar for each one.
When the timer ends, stop, assess and decide deliberately whether to book another block.

trap: Packing the calendar edge to edge with no buffers, so one delay cascades through the whole schedule.
procedureFull:
1. Identify the top 1–3 prioritized deliverables for the day.
2. Estimate an aggressive yet realistic duration for each deliverable based on decomposed sub-tasks.
3. Open the calendar and assign non-overlapping, explicit calendar events for each task block.
4. Treat each block as a deterministic production sprint: when the timer expires, halt work, assess status, and deliberately decide whether to allocate another explicit box or transition.
setupFull:
Daily Schedule: 2026-11-04
  * 08:30 - 10:00 [DEEP WORK] Core Engine Parser Optimization
  * 10:00 - 10:15 [INTERSTITIAL] Rest & Physical Hydration
  * 10:15 - 11:45 [DEEP WORK] AST Node Generation Implementation
  * 11:45 - 12:45 [RECOVERY] Lunch & Aerobic Walking
  * 12:45 - 13:30 [BATCH ADMIN] Email triage, PR reviews, Slack
  * 13:30 - 15:00 [MEETINGS] Engineering sync & architecture review
trapFull: Underestimating temporal friction and packing calendars edge-to-edge without buffers. This causes single-point delays to cascade throughout the entire schedule.
